title: Tamarin Theories Accompanying "Trust No Pool: Formal Security Analysis of BPMN Collaborations" (BPM 2026)
description:
This artifact accompanies the paper "Trust No Pool: Formal Security Analysis of BPMN Collaborations" by Martin Farkas and Imre Kocsis, accepted at the 24th International Conference on Business Process Management (BPM 2026), Track I (Foundations).

It contains the Tamarin prover theories and automation scripts used to formally verify (or refute) security properties of a four-pool BPMN procurement collaboration under multiple platform enforcement profiles.

Scope. 20 verification configurations: four platform enforcement profiles — loose coupling (Pi_LC), smart-contract orchestration (Pi_SC), Verifiable Credential–based self-orchestration (Pi_VC), and the full Dolev-Yao network adversary (Pi_DY) — crossed with four adversarial pool designations (Procurement Authority, Regulatory Authority, Supplier A, Supplier B), plus the honest secure-channel baseline (Pi_0). The Pi_VC profile is parameterised by atomic vs. non-atomic Verifiable Data Registry semantics, isolating a time-of-check-to-time-of-use behaviour.

Lemmas. Six security lemmas: no bifurcation (G1), non-repudiation (G2), faithful history (G3), authorized progression (G4), instance isolation (G7), value secrecy (G6a).

Requirements. Tamarin prover 1.8.0 or later, Bash 4+, Linux/macOS/WSL. On a 12-core x86 machine with 96 GB RAM the full suite completes in under two minutes.

The methodology builds on prior work by the same authors on Verifiable Credential–based self-orchestration of business collaborations (BPM 2025).
